How one request moves.

Every part of StrayPaw is a step in one chain. A message on WhatsApp is where it starts.

A report arrives
On WhatsApp or the web: a photo, a place and what was seen. The reporter is never shown publicly.
It becomes a case
An organisation accepts it, and from then on someone owns it. The reporter sees when it is accepted.
Care is recorded once
Treatment, sterilisation, vaccination and follow-ups are written to the case as the work happens.
The animal keeps its history
Everything done lands on one StrayPaw ID, so the next team starts where the last one stopped.
The map updates
The area the animal lives in reflects the record, with unknowns drawn as unknown.
The city sees the pattern
Requests, care and gaps add up area by area into a brief a municipal team can act on.
The work becomes evidence

title: Our Story, StrayPaw
h1: Every street animal deserves a history. So we are building one.
text:
Hanging (Palampore), late 17th century · The Metropolitan Museum of Art (CC0)

Our Story

Every street animal deserves a history. So we are building one.

StrayPaw is a technology company building the shared information and coordination infrastructure for street-animal care in India.

Explore the platform
Contact us
01
The problem, in one number.

One rescue register brought into StrayPaw held 169 open requests, and no column for who was responsible for them.

Every request had been seen by someone; none had an owner. Care is repeated or missed. Funders cannot see what worked. Cities plan sterilisation and response without knowing where help is needed.

02
Mission and vision.
Mission
Make street-animal care more coordinated, accountable and informed, through technology anyone can use.
Vision
The shared information and coordination infrastructure connecting animals, communities, care organisations and cities.
03
Six rules the software keeps.
Unknown is not zero
A place with no records is not recorded, never no animals.
Not examined is an answer
Sterilisation and vaccination have three states, not two.
A rate names its base
Shares are shown against the animals checked, and against all on record.
Someone owns every case
A report reaches a queue only when an organisation takes it on.

title: For funders, fund an outcome, not a hope
text:
Fund an outcome,
not a hope.

Most animal-welfare giving buys activity: a number of surgeries, a number of camps. What it rarely buys is the ability to say afterwards whether the population actually changed. That is a measurement problem, and it is fixable.

FUND
STUDY
ACT
MEASURE
EVIDENCE RETURNS TO THE NEXT DECISION
Activity is easy to buy. Change is not.

Sterilisation only reduces a population if it clears a coverage threshold in a defined area. Below it, animals are replaced faster than they are treated: real welfare benefit for individual dogs, no population effect. Both outcomes are reported the same way, as a count of surgeries.

A question, a partner, and a finish line.
01
Define

You bring an objective and a geography. We turn it into a scoped question with a real denominator, or, where none exists, a baseline study to establish one first.

02
Cost

Unit costs are published and sourced, not quoted. You see the arithmetic: animals, rate, duration, field teams, before anything is committed.

03
Execute

A named local organisation does the fieldwork. The study design, the data tooling and the record layer come from StrayPaw.

04
Verify

Outcomes post to the animal records as they happen. At the end you get coverage measured against the baseline, not a count of activity.
